title: Best Boutique Hotels in Phoenix: 10 Distinctive Stays in and Around the City
description:
For this guide, I am using Phoenix the way travelers often search it: Phoenix proper plus the nearby boutique-hotel orbit of Paradise Valley and close-in Scottsdale. That matters because several of the region’s best boutique stays sit just beyond city limits, but they compete directly with Phoenix hotels for the same romantic weekends, design-forward escapes, and special occasion trips.

My quickest recommendation: If I wanted the best boutique hotel in Phoenix proper, I would book Royal Palms Resort and Spa. It feels romantic, historically rooted, and unusually transportive without leaving the city. If I wanted the most intimate boutique experience near Phoenix, I would choose The Hermosa Inn. If I wanted something more urban and artsy, FOUND: RE Phoenix would be my first stop.

” A property needed to offer several of the following: A clear and memorable design identity Strong local character, history, art, or architecture A more intimate or experience-led feel than a standard chain hotel Distinctive room concepts, such as casitas, bungalows, villas, individually styled rooms, or historic layouts A stay that feels worth choosing because of the property itself, not only because of the location That is why this guide includes two kinds of properties: True boutique hotels and inns, such as The Hermosa Inn, Bespoke Inn Scottsdale, FOUND: RE Phoenix, and RISE Uptown Hotel Boutique-style resorts that are larger but still highly individual, such as Royal Palms, Mountain Shadows, Andaz Scottsdale, Hotel Valley Ho, and The Scott Resort & Spa I left out enormous conventional resorts, even if they are beautiful, because that would turn this from a boutique guide into a luxury-resort list wearing different jewelry.

title: Richmond's Boutique Hotels: Art, History & Design
description:
Downtown Richmond offers a collection of boutique hotels that blend historic architecture with modern design. Expect properties like the Linden Row Inn, a pre-Civil War row of seven homes now operating as a boutique inn, and the art-focused Quirk Hotel Richmond with its rotating gallery and rooftop bar. Most are within walking distance of the Virginia State Capitol, the Greater Richmond Convention Center, and the James River waterfront.

Room rates generally range from moderate to upscale, with average nightly prices between $150 and $300 depending on season and amenities. Top-rated options include the Quirk Hotel Richmond (bcom score 82, Very Good) offering bathrobes, a fitness center, and a lobby bar; the historic Linden Row Inn (85, Fabulous) with period furnishings and free access to a nearby YMCA health club; and the Delta Hotels by Marriott Richmond Downtown (83, Very Good) overlooking the James River with an indoor pool and sauna.

title: Best Hotels in Richmond, VA - Find My Food Stu
description:
Best Hotels in Richmond, VA: Where to Stay Finding the best hotels in Richmond, VA starts with knowing which part of the city fits your trip. As the capital of Virginia, Richmond sits along the James River, with scenic river walks, a compact downtown packed with Civil War history, museums, and historic architecture, and suburban areas like Short Pump offering easy access to shopping and dining outside the city core. Beyond the historic sites, Richmond has a genuinely strong food and drink scene.

The area is home to several of Richmond’s most well-known hotels, including the historic Jefferson Hotel, the boutique Linden Row Inn, and newer options like The Moxy and Quirk Hotel. Major cultural institutions nearby include the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts, the American Civil War Museum, and the Poe Museum. The broader downtown area takes in Monroe Ward, Shockoe Slip, Shockoe Bottom, and Jackson Ward.

Hotels here lean practical rather than boutique. The Hilton Richmond Hotel & Spa is the most upscale option in the area, with a full-service spa and solid amenities. Hyatt House is a strong mid-range pick, especially for families or extended stays. Budget options like Holiday Inn Express are also well represented. Short Pump is best for visitors prioritizing convenience, shopping, or business travel over walkability or historic character.

LUXURY The Jefferson Hotel www.jeffersonhotel.com Downtown The Jefferson is the standout luxury hotel in Richmond and one of the most historically significant hotels on the East Coast. Open since 1895, the property features marble floors, stained-glass windows, and Beaux Arts architecture that landed it on the National Register of Historic Places in 1969. Presidents from Benjamin Harrison to Barack Obama have stayed here, along with a long list of world leaders, actors, and authors.
